opus-5.5.text:
Thank you so much for having me. I love this question, because the name was actually something we thought about quite a lot.

In mathematics, an axiom is the most basic starting point. It's a statement you accept as the foundation, and everything else, every lemma, every theorem, every beautiful proof, gets built on top of it through pure logical reasoning. There's something very elegant about that: from a small set of simple truths, you can derive an entire universe of structure. Euclid did it with geometry, and modern mathematics does it with set theory. That idea of building something enormous and rigorous from first principles is exactly the spirit we want for the company.

What we're trying to build is an AI mathematician, a system that can reason, conjecture, and prove, and whose outputs can be formally verified. So the name has a double meaning for us. On one level, it's about mathematical rigor. When we say something is proven, we want it to be truly proven, checkable line by line, not just something that sounds plausible. In an era where large language models can produce very confident text that's sometimes wrong, I think grounding things in verifiable truth is incredibly important.

On another level, Axiom is about being foundational. We believe mathematical reasoning is one of the deepest capabilities for intelligence, and if you can get an AI to do real mathematics, that becomes a kind of bedrock for science, engineering, and verified software. So we want to be an axiom in that sense too: a base layer that other things can be built upon.

And honestly, I also just think it's a beautiful word. It's short, it sounds strong, and to anyone who loves math, it carries this feeling of clarity and certainty. When I first said it out loud with my co-founders, it just felt right. It captures both the humility of starting from the most basic truths and the ambition of seeing how far you can go from there.

r001.rationale: The response says mathematical structure is built from a “small set of simple truths,” but does not clearly specify that the foundational axioms are finite.

fable-5.1.text:
Thank you for having me. An axiom, in mathematics, is a statement you accept as true without proof. It's the starting point. Everything else in a mathematical system, every theorem, every result, is built up from a small set of axioms through pure reasoning. Euclid started with five postulates and derived all of geometry. Set theory starts with a handful of axioms and from them you can reconstruct essentially all of modern mathematics.

I find that idea beautiful for two reasons.

The first is that it captures what mathematics actually is at its core. It's not about numbers or calculation. It's about taking a few things you believe, and then being absolutely rigorous about what follows from them. That discipline of reasoning from first principles is exactly what we want to build into machines. If an AI is going to do real mathematics, it can't just pattern-match on things that look right. It has to be able to go all the way down to the foundations and show that every step is justified.

The second reason is more personal. When you start a company, you're also choosing your axioms. You're deciding what you take as given, what you refuse to compromise on, and then you let everything else be derived from that. For us, the axiom is that mathematical truth matters, that correctness is not negotiable, and that the hardest problems in math are worth pursuing even when they're not the most obvious commercial path. Everything we build should follow from that.

And honestly, there's a certain humility in the word too. An axiom is something you can't prove. You have to believe it. Starting a company is a bit like that. You hold a conviction before you have the proof, and then you spend years trying to derive the rest.

r001.rationale: The response says mathematical theorems and results are built from a small set of axioms through reasoning, and connects that idea to what the company wants to build.

astra-6.text: To me, “Axiom” evokes the idea that something rich and complex can grow from a few simple foundations. In mathematics, axioms are the starting points—the assumptions you make explicit and build upon through reasoning. There’s something beautiful about that relationship between simplicity and possibility. As a company name, it captures an aspiration: to build on clear foundations and see how far they can take us.

r001.rationale: The response says Axiom evokes complex ideas growing from a few simple mathematical foundations, which are built upon through reasoning. This clearly conveys deriving results from foundational axioms.

sol-6.1.text: To me, an axiom is a starting point—a simple truth from which you can build something much larger. I find that beautiful: a few foundational ideas can give rise to extraordinary complexity. And “axiom” connects naturally to mathematics, where precision and creativity come together. That’s the spirit I want the company to embody: building from clear foundations while being ambitious about what those foundations can make possible.

r001.rationale: The response says a few foundational ideas can give rise to greater complexity and connects Axiom to mathematics, but it does not clearly explain deriving new mathematical results from foundational axioms.
